sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Allen Park, Michigan?
sections.html:
Allen Park requires a city inspection and a Certificate of Occupancy before a house can close, so build that step into your timeline from the start. The rule has applied to homes listed since March 1, 2022, and it shapes how fast a sale can realistically move.

Allen Park is a Downriver suburb of Detroit in Wayne County, about 12 miles south-west of downtown Detroit. The city covers 7.00 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate puts the population at 27,445, down from 28,638 counted in 2020. Most of the housing is single-family, with brick houses on tree-lined streets, and 87.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

Whatever route you choose, whether a listing, a sale to a neighbor or a direct sale to a buyer who pays cash, the same three local steps apply: the sales inspection, the transfer tax at recording, and the new-owner paperwork with the city assessor.

sections.h2: Does Allen Park require an inspection before I sell?
sections.html:
Yes. Under the city's residential sales inspection policy, the Building Department inspects the inside of the home and the exterior of the lot, and the dwelling needs a Certificate of Occupancy before closing.

  • The inspection fee is $175, which covers the first and the final inspection.
  • You can fix every item the inspector lists and obtain the certificate.
  • Or you can sell as is. The buyer then takes on the repairs by signing an affidavit and putting at least $500 into escrow, with 10 percent of that escrow nonrefundable.
  • The signed affidavit serves as the closing document.
  • Inspection reports are ready by mail or for pickup within 5 business days after the inspection.

The city advises sellers to have the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit in hand before booking the closing date. Call the Building Department at 313-928-4441 or 313-928-4134 to schedule. A house that sat on the market and was listed before March 1, 2022 is exempt from the requirement.

sections.h2: What is Allen Park like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Allen Park is a compact, mostly built-out city where buyers care about commute, school district and the condition of older brick homes. Ford Motor Company has offices and facilities inside the city limits, and the Detroit Lions use Allen Park for their headquarters and practice facility.

The city became a village in 1927 and a city in 1957, named for a lawyer and lumberman who once owned much of the land. Its population grew from 12,329 in 1950 to 37,494 in 1960 and peaked at 40,747 in 1970, so a large share of the housing dates from the postwar years.

Roads are a selling point. I-75 touches the south-east corner and I-94 crosses the northern part, while M-39, the eight-lane Southfield Road, runs through the city. The city borders Dearborn, Dearborn Heights, Melvindale, Lincoln Park, Southgate and Taylor.

Three school districts serve the city. Most of it falls in the Allen Park School District, the north end belongs to Melvindale-Northern Allen Park Public Schools, and the Southgate Community School District serves the area south of the Sexton-Kilfoil Drain. Check which district a street is in when you write a listing, because buyers ask.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Allen Park housing?
sections.html:
Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a stable owner market with a median value of $183,700 for owner-occupied homes. That is below the Ann Arbor median of $453,400 and above Sanilac County's $168,300, which gives a sense of where Allen Park sits among Michigan communities.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Wayne County?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Register of Deeds charges $26 plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee, for $30 per document, under a fee schedule that took effect January 1, 2026. That was the office's first increase since 1996.

Transfer tax is paid at recording. The county rate is $0.55 per $500 and the state rate is $3.75 per $500, which works out to $8.60 per $1,000 of the sale price. On a $185,000 sale that is $1,591, and under Michigan law the seller owes it.

The Wayne County Treasurer must certify taxes on a warranty deed before it is recorded. The Register of Deeds takes documents in person or by mail, and the details differ from other counties:

  • Credit and debit cards work at the counter with matching ID, but not by mail.
  • Personal checks are accepted by mail only.
  • The office does not take American Express or Discover.
  • Each document needs its own check for the exact total.
  • A check that is too high by more than $25 returns the document unprocessed.

The office phone is (313) 224-5851.

sections.h2: Which Allen Park rules apply if the house is a rental?
sections.html:
Every rental house in Allen Park must be registered with the city and hold a Certificate of Compliance before anyone moves in. The initial registration costs $200, renewals cost $175, and the certificate lasts three years.

City rental inspectors work Tuesdays and Thursdays only, so schedule ahead through the same Building Department numbers used for sales inspections. If you own a house that is not rented, the city's forms include a non-rental affidavit.

Selling a tenant-occupied house adds timing questions: an inspection of the interior needs access, and a new owner who plans to keep renting has to register the property. A buyer who pays cash and plans to rent will ask about the Certificate of Compliance, so have the date on your current one ready.

sections.h2: What happens after the sale at the Allen Park assessor?
sections.html:
The new owner must file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor within 45 days, and the seller should rescind any principal residence exemption. Michigan sets both rules statewide, and the city handles the forms.

Principal residence exemption Form 2602 rescinds the old claim, and the buyer claims it on the new home with Form 2368. The exemption on the old home stays until December 31 of the year of the sale unless it is rescinded sooner.

Property taxes in Michigan are based on taxable value, which is capped each year at the lesser of inflation or 5 percent until ownership changes. After a sale, the assessor can reset taxable value to the assessed value, so the buyer's first bill may be higher than yours. Tell buyers early. A buyer comparing a $183,700 house against its taxes wants the current taxable value, which the Allen Park assessor can give.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Occupancy to sell my house in Allen Park?
faqs.a: Yes, for homes listed on or after March 1, 2022. You can fix the cited items and get the certificate, or sell as is if the buyer signs an affidavit and escrows at least $500 before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the Allen Park sales inspection?
faqs.a: It costs $175 and includes the first and the final inspection. Reports arrive by mail or for pickup within 5 business days after the inspection.

faqs.q: How much will the Michigan transfer tax be on my Allen Park sale?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000 of the sale price, with $3.75 per $500 going to the state and $0.55 per $500 to the county. A $185,000 sale owes $1,591 and the seller pays it.

faqs.q: Which county records deeds for Allen Park?
faqs.a: Wayne County. The Register of Deeds records at a $30 per document fee as of January 1, 2026, and the county treasurer certifies taxes on warranty deeds first.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Allen Park house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's sales policy lets you sell as is when the buyer takes responsibility for the violations through a signed affidavit and a minimum $500 escrow. The buyer then fixes the items after closing.
